extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation. It comprises 1,825 diverse executable queries across nine domains (Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications, Simulations, Data Science, Management Systems, Multimedia Editing, Quick Tools, and Others), stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers. The framework renders each artifact and captures its dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots, assessed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge guided by fine-grained, per-task checklists. It evaluates over 30 leading LLMs and achieves 94.4% ranking consistency with WebDev Arena and up to 90.95% pairwise agreement with human experts.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team. ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv:2507.04952v2 [cs.CL], 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities, LLM-drafted and then human-refined.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control: (i) MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce a 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability. LLM rewriting added diverse styles with human verification. Solvability validation collected candidate solutions from multiple model families and pruned underspecified items. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Execution was standardized with headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024x768 resolution with deterministic seeds, capturing three staged screenshots (before/during/after scripted interaction).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities (five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions). Checklists were generated by Hunyuan-Turbos and human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators; the seed was reused as few-shot references. Each dimension is scored on a 10-point scale with detailed rubrics. For human validation, 280 queries with data from 6 models were independently scored by multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience following a double-blind protocol; the final human ground-truth score represents the median of individual annotators' ratings.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 was achieved among annotators for checklist calibration. Pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) was used to quantify agreement between the automated MLLM referee and human experts. The dual-referee setup (Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B) induced highly consistent partial-order constraints over model rankings. Residual differences concentrated among top systems. Replacing the deprecated Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with the stable Gemini-2.5-Pro left conclusions unchanged.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 checklist dimensions per query; human validation used multiple annotators per item (median score used as ground truth)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini-2.5-Pro (MLLM-as-Judge referee), Qwen2.5-VL-72B (MLLM-as-Judge referee), Hunyuan-Turbos (checklist generation), Gemini-2.5-Pro (query classification), Playwright/headless Chromium (artifact execution and screenshot capture)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. Dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released. Future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The quality filtering prompt explicitly checks for privacy: queries must avoid requesting or involving any sensitive personal information, such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: ArtifactsBench aims to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models by providing a scalable and accurate evaluation tool. It addresses the gap between LLM code generation capabilities and real-world user experience quality, enabling better assessment of interactive visual artifacts central to modern applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark currently focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn, which does not assess agentic or iterative development capabilities. The discrete screenshot sampling approach may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior by capturing and analyzing a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions (e.g., multi-step user workflows, nuanced physics in games). The benchmark does not assess an LLM's capability to function as an autonomous agent that iteratively refines artifacts based on feedback or debugs its own code. Evaluation is limited to single-turn artifact generation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking LLMs on interactive visual code generation tasks. The benchmark supports fine-grained capability analysis across nine domains and three difficulty tiers (Easy/Medium/Hard). It is designed for automated, holistic, and reproducible evaluation of LLM-generated interactive visual artifacts, providing diagnostic insights on model strengths and failure modes.
